Guide word

Parameter

A pair that means nothing physical is skipped; a pair with a ▶ OTS test can be run on the DCS.

Left to right, in this order

Consequences

Risk · interactive

Severity × likelihood

Risk = S × L, judged after the safeguards; High and Very high need an action.

Worked example N2 · interactive

V-201, eleven rows

Only N2.3 ranks High (S4 × L3 = 12): it is the row that goes to LOPA.

▶ OTS chip

Test a row on the DCS

  • Press ▶ OTS on a row: the deviation starts after one minute.
  • The panel lists alarms, trips and key tags as they come.
  • Compare with the consequences you wrote; edit the row.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • A deviation is a guide word applied to a parameter of one node.
  • Consequences are written before any safeguard is credited.
  • Risk = S × L in four bands; High rows need an action.
  • ▶ OTS shows whether the safeguards act as written.

Part 3 · LOPA and the hand-in

Are the safeguards enough?

Part 3 · the plan

From a High row to a number

S × L ranks a row; LOPA says by how much the layers fall short.

  1. The symbolsfrequencies, probabilities and the target
  2. The chainunmitigated, mitigated, compared with TEL
  3. Row N2.3 by LOPAwhich layers count, and the gap
  4. Hand-inreport, Excel and the saved study

LOPA · symbols

What goes into the Full worksheet

\(f_{IE}\)
initiating-event frequency (sum if several)
/yr
\(P_{EN},\ P_{CM}\)
enabling condition; conditional modifier (e.g. people present)
–
\(PFD_i\)
failure on demand of IPL \(i\), from the safeguard list
–
\(f_{unmit},\ f_{mit}\)
consequence frequency without, with the IPLs
/yr
TEL
tolerable frequency for S: S4 = 10⁻³, S5 = 10⁻⁴
/yr

LOPA · derivation

Three multiplications and a comparison

\(f_{unmit} = f_{IE}\,P_{EN}\,P_{CM}\)how often the consequence starts
\(f_{mit} = f_{unmit}\,\prod_i PFD_i\)each IPL must also fail
\(\mathrm{RRF} = f_{mit}/\mathrm{TEL},\quad \mathrm{RRR} = \mathrm{TEL}/f_{mit}\)if \(f_{mit} > \mathrm{TEL}\): the gap, and the PFD a new layer needs

These are PHA Studio's definitions, shown step by step in its LOPA panel.

LOPA · interactive

Move the inputs, watch the gap

\(f_{mit} = f_{IE}\,P_{EN}\,P_{CM}\prod_i PFD_i\)

Each tenfold layer moves \(f_{mit}\) one decade down; the defaults are row N2.3.

Worked row N2.3 · interactive

Which layers may be credited?

The level alarm leaves 2 min to carry-over, too little for an operator, so only LSHH-215 counts.

Full edition

LOPA columns, groups, the hand-in

  • Scenario groups: one LOPA for rows that share a consequence.
  • Check and report: open fields, then Word report and Excel.
  • Workshop mode: projector view; phones send ideas.
  • File ▸ Save: one .json per group to hand in.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • \(f_{mit}\) = initiating frequency × conditions × each IPL's PFD.
  • Compare with TEL; RRF is the gap, RRR the PFD a new layer needs.
  • N2.3: 4.5 × 10⁻³ /yr against 10⁻³ /yr, a gap of 4.5.
  • Hand in the report, the Excel and the saved .json.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

State the node's design intent before any deviation.

2

Write consequences with no safeguard credited.

3

Run the row on the OTS and correct what you wrote.

4

Credit an IPL only if it is independent and fast enough.

5

Save the study as .json; that file is the hand-in.
